channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Ex-Police Colonel Jailed for 6 Years and 8 Months for Fraud
item.description: A former police colonel, Alimzhan Kadyrov, has been sentenced to 6 years and 8 months in prison in Almaty for fraud. He posed as a relative of former National Security Committee head Karim Massimov, promising to resolve complex issues in state bodies. The investigation spanned over five years, involving four episodes of deception.

item.title: Almaty Offers Free Public Transport on Election Day
item.description: Almaty will provide free public transportation on Sunday due to the upcoming maslikhat elections. The city administration announced this measure to facilitate voter access to polling stations across the city.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry Urges Students to Prioritize Safety Over Institutional Reputation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs stressed that educational institutions must not prioritize their reputation over student safety. The ministry urged students to report violence and extortion, and university administrations to act on these reports. Joint efforts by police, akimats, and universities are underway to prevent offenses, violence, and bullying.

item.title: Man in Zhambyl Region Owes 3.2 Million Tenge in Alimony
item.description: A resident of the Zhambyl region has been found to owe 3.2 million Tenge in alimony for his child. The prosecutor's office initiated a pre-trial investigation after the man failed to meet his obligations since 2023. The debtor confessed, paid the full amount, and promised to fulfill his obligations, leading to the case's dismissal under amnesty.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Ban on Energy Drinks Starting 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a ban on the import, production, storage, sale, and consumption of energy drinks from January 1, 2027. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce developed the bill to protect public health, especially for children and adolescents, by preventing related illnesses. The ban applies to non-alcoholic and low-alcohol beverages with caffeine concentrations exceeding 150 mg/liter and containing specific energy-boosting substances.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Assistive Technologies for Independent Living of People with Disabilities
item.description: A committee meeting was held at Astana Hub to discuss assistive technologies for the independent living of people with disabilities. The focus was on domestic prototypes and their transition to production. As of October 1, 2026, over 762,400 people with disabilities were registered in Kazakhstan. The meeting proposed improving legislation, developing a roadmap for testing and implementing innovations, and strengthening the link between science and production.

item.title: Drug Dealers Arrested in Tashkent, One Hid Narcotics in Child's Hat
item.description: Tashkent police arrested two suspected drug dealers involved in illegal drug trafficking. In one incident, a man attempted to hide narcotics in his three-year-old son's hat during a traffic stop. Another suspect was apprehended with two drug packages and confessed to distributing 28 ' закладки' (hidden drug stashes). Both individuals have been detained, and criminal cases have been initiated.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Up to 30% Increase in Heating Tariffs Due to Rising Costs
item.description: Uzbekistan's heating supply company, Issiqlikta'minot, is proposing a tariff increase of up to 30%. The company cited rising gas, electricity, and water prices as reasons for the potential hike. Digitalization and a shift to alternative energy sources are seen as ways to reduce production costs, but these measures take time. Some regional tariffs have not been revised in years.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry Addresses Student Safety After Campus Incidents
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has issued an appeal to students and university leaders to prevent violence, bullying, and other offenses on campuses. Police are working with local authorities and universities to ensure student safety. Since the start of the academic year, 566 offenses have been intercepted, including violations of migration laws. Police officers are assigned to dormitories, and security measures have been enhanced.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Limiting Car Traffic by Odd/Even Dates During Poor Air Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering implementing traffic restrictions for vehicles based on odd and even license plate numbers when air quality deteriorates. Other proposed measures include reducing industrial output, temporarily halting construction, and alerting the public via SMS. These steps aim to mitigate the impact of high levels of air pollution.

item.title: Two Uzbek Citizens Among Five Killed in Almaty Residential Fire
item.description: Two citizens of Uzbekistan were among the five people, including a child, who died in a fire at a private residential building in Almaty. The cause of death for the Uzbek nationals was carbon monoxide poisoning. Uzbekistan's Consulate General in Almaty is coordinating with local authorities for the repatriation of the bodies. An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Conversion of 17 Hectares of Arable Land in Osh for Housing Complex
item.description: The Kyrgyz cabinet has approved the conversion of 17.2 hectares of irrigated arable land in Osh for the construction of the "Ene-Sai City" multifunctional residential complex. Three land plots will be reclassified from agricultural to settlement lands. The Osh mayor's office is tasked with ensuring targeted use, developing urban planning documentation, and compensating for agricultural losses.

item.title: Eight Individuals Arrested in Zhambyl Region for Alimony Debt
item.description: Eight individuals in the Zhambyl region have been arrested for failing to pay alimony. The regional prosecutor's office reported that 14 debtors faced administrative action, with eight arrested and six fined. One resident accumulated a debt of 3.2 million tenge for child support since 2023.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China Discuss Opening 'Green Corridors' for Border Cargo
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and China are considering opening 'green corridors' for specific categories of cargo across their shared border. This initiative was discussed on November 25 in Shanghai during the first meeting of the Kyrgyz-Chinese committee on border crossing management. The parties signed a protocol, aiming to increase border crossing capacity and modernize infrastructure.

item.title: Astana Lawyer Sentenced to Two Years for Attempted Fraud
item.description: A lawyer in Astana has been sentenced to two years in prison for attempted fraud. The lawyer had demanded 7 million tenge from a client, promising to secure her release from custody under house arrest. The client reported the incident to law enforcement, leading to the lawyer's arrest. The court also banned him from practicing law for six years.

item.title: Kabul Bank Chairman Appoints Own Watchdog Amid Oversight Dispute
item.description: Khyber Omarkhail, Chairman of Kabul Bank's Management Board, has allegedly acted against banking principles by retaining Ahmad Shakil Hazem on the Board of Supervisors, refusing a replacement nominated by the Ministry of Finance. Sources claim Omarkhail's actions, including blocking the new nominee Sameer Razavi, are due to ethnic considerations and an attempt to prevent independent oversight.

item.title: Four Dead as Car Plunges into Panj River in Tajikistan's Darvaz District
item.description: A Toyota Verso vehicle fell into the Panj River in Tajikistan's Darvaz district, resulting in the deaths of the driver and three passengers. Another passenger sustained severe injuries. The accident occurred on November 26 on the Dushanbe-Khorog highway. The driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle, causing it to fall approximately 70-80 meters into the river.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Adjusts Conditions for Free Wheelchair Provision
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has amended social security regulations, lowering the age limit for free wheelchairs from 85 to 75 years. Changes also affect the Republican Center for Medico-Social Expertise, introducing a deputy director position. Individuals with unexpunged convictions are now barred from directing social institutions for vulnerable groups.

item.title: Hackers Breach US Air Force Cloud Platform, Risking Sensitive Military Data
item.description: Hackers have gained access to a US Air Force cloud computing platform, raising concerns about the potential exposure of classified military information. The timing and extent of the breach remain unclear, according to NBC News. The Air Force stated it continuously takes measures to protect its information and systems.

item.title: Afghan Diplomatic Missions Condemn Taliban Killing of Six Panjshir Youths
item.description: The Coordination Council of Afghanistan’s Diplomatic and Consular Missions has condemned the killing of six young men from Panjshir by the Taliban. The council called for an independent investigation by UN bodies, citing concerns about arbitrary violations of the right to life and extrajudicial executions. They urged the immediate return of bodies and evidence collection.

item.title: Eurasian Development Bank to Invest Up to $3 Billion in Uzbekistan Over Five Years
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) plans to invest up to $3 billion in Uzbekistan's economy between 2027 and 2031, potentially reaching $5-6 billion with additional investors. The bank's country strategy aligns with Uzbekistan's 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy, focusing on industry, infrastructure, finance, digital economy, and transport.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Condemns 'Systematic Killing' of Panjshiri Residents by Taliban
item.description: Afghanistan's UN envoy, the National Resistance Front, and the Freedom Front of Afghanistan have condemned the killing of six young men from Panjshir in Kabul by the Taliban, calling it a "systematic and deliberate killing" of Panjshiri residents. The envoy urged independent investigation and accountability for perpetrators.

item.title: Europe Sees 16% Rise in Russia-Linked Sabotage Incidents, IISS Reports
item.description: Europe has experienced a 16% increase in sabotage incidents linked to Russia, according to the IISS. Germany and Poland are likely to remain primary targets due to their crucial role in supplying military aid to Ukraine via their transport, logistics, and industrial sectors.

item.title: Modernized Border Crossing Points Open Between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
item.description: Modernized border crossing points between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have been opened. The upgrade aims to improve efficiency and capacity at these key transit locations, facilitating smoother movement of people and goods across the shared border.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Restoration of Fatkhobod Hydropower Plant Damaged by Flood
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources visited the Fatkhobod small hydropower plant to assess damage from a 2024 flood. The plant, built in 2010, was temporarily suspended after floodwaters damaged its structures. Discussions focused on repair and recommissioning.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Invest Trillions of Tenge in Transit Corridor Upgrades
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate over 2 trillion tenge for the development of transit road corridors within the next three years. The Ministry of Transport detailed plans to improve routes like "Aktobe – Kyzylorda" and "Beyneu – Saksaulsky." Additionally, 37 border crossing points within the EAEU will be modernized by 2027 to double throughput capacity.

item.title: Kuwait Summons Iran's Ambassador After Deadly Drone Attack
item.description: Kuwait's Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's ambassador to protest "continuous Iranian attacks," including a recent drone strike that killed two Italian citizens. Iran has denied involvement, with its Foreign Minister offering cooperation to determine the incident's origin. The attack targeted a vital facility, also injuring a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 60th Globally in Global Knowledge Index, Excels in Early Childhood and Secondary Education
item.description: Kazakhstan achieved a score of 48.1 out of 100 in the Global Knowledge Index, securing 60th place among 155 countries. The nation particularly excelled in early childhood and secondary education, ranking 19th globally in this category. The index was developed by the UN Development Programme and the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation.

item.title: Tajikistan Approves State Program for Cryosphere Study and Glacier Preservation (2026-2030)
item.description: The Tajik government has approved a State Program for the Study of the Cryosphere and Glacier Preservation for 2026-2030. The program aims to enhance cryosphere research, improve glacier monitoring, strengthen scientific capacity, and better assess climate and natural risks, including glacial lake outburst floods.

item.title: 98-Year-Old Kazakh Man Undergoes Successful Heart Valve Replacement in Almaty
item.description: Doctors at the Institute of Cardiology and Internal Diseases in Almaty successfully replaced the heart valve of a 98-year-old patient in a 45-minute minimally invasive procedure. The patient, diagnosed with aortic stenosis, received a new valve via a small incision in the thigh, significantly improving blood flow without open-chest surgery.

item.title: Astana Lawyer Sentenced to Two Years for Attempting to Defraud Client
item.description: An Astana lawyer has been sentenced to two years in prison for attempting to defraud a client by claiming to have connections in government agencies. The lawyer demanded 7 million tenge to allegedly resolve a case, but the client reported the scheme to law enforcement, leading to the lawyer's arrest and conviction.

item.title: CIA Documents Suggest Son-in-Law of Afghan Leader Waterboarded in Kabul
item.description: Newly released CIA documents, obtained through a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit, suggest that Ghairat Bahir, the son-in-law of former Afghan Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, was waterboarded at a secret CIA detention facility in Kabul in 2012. A former CIA contract interpreter reportedly witnessed the incident, describing a detainee being strapped to a board and subjected to waterboarding.

item.title: Bishkek Eco-Plant Processes Over 400,000 Tons of Waste in First Year
item.description: Bishkek's waste incineration plant processed 401,500 tons of waste and generated 187.9 million kWh of electricity in its first year of operation. The facility currently handles 1,000 to 1,200 tons of solid waste daily, with a power generation capacity of 30 MW. Authorities plan to triple the plant's capacity by constructing a second unit, which will increase total waste processing to 3,000 tons per day and electricity generation to 90 MW.

item.title: Almaty's Transport Woes Linked to Urban Planning, Not Just Population Growth
item.description: Traffic jams and crowded buses are a daily reality in Almaty. Experts suggest that beyond population increase, the city's spatial planning and transport system are key factors. Despite a lower population density than other global megacities, Almaty struggles with public transport, with about a million people using it daily amidst over a million cars.

item.title: US Central Command Refutes Iranian Navy's Claims of Attacking US Aircraft Carrier
item.description: US Central Command (CENTCOM) has labeled claims by Iran's Navy Commander Shahram Irani, stating Iran targeted the USS Abraham Lincoln, as false. CENTCOM asserted the USS Abraham Lincoln returned to the US last month after a successful deployment and described other Iranian official remarks as fabricated lies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Resizes Protected Zones Around Issyk-Kul for 'Ala-Too Resort' Project
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has altered the functional zoning of the Issyk-Kul biosphere territory to facilitate the 'Ala-Too Resort' project. The buffer zone's area is reduced by over 5,000 hectares, with an equivalent increase in the transitional zone, which now includes land designated for the resort.

item.title: Ukraine Submits Proposals for Black Sea Grain Deal, Awaiting Moscow's Response
item.description: Ukraine has sent its proposals for a Black Sea grain deal to partners and is awaiting Moscow's response. Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba stated Ukraine is ready for a deal and thanked mediators like India, Turkey, and Egypt. Russia reportedly seeks to include oil in any grain agreement.

item.title: Afghanistan's Foreign Minister Criticizes Pakistan's Policy as Failed
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, Afghanistan's Foreign Minister, stated that Pakistan's policy towards Afghanistan has been unreasonable and unsuccessful. He rejected Pakistan's claims of TTP operating from Afghan territory and urged Islamabad to reconsider its approach, emphasizing that historical attempts to impose will on Afghanistan by force have failed.

item.title: Almaty Residents Oppose Construction Near Cyran Lake Due to Safety Concerns
item.description: Residents near Almaty's Cyran Lake are concerned about the safety of four under-construction apartment buildings. They fear soil subsidence and potential sliding of the high-rises towards the lake, which could endanger nearby homes. Despite identified violations, construction continues.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Post-2030 Development Agenda with International Experts
item.description: Kazakhstan participated in an international seminar in Geneva discussing the post-2030 sustainable development agenda. Minister S. Nurbek emphasized practical solutions and the role of science and AI. E. Kazhykhan highlighted the importance of a new UN global agenda and Kazakhstan's initiative for a UN Regional Center in Almaty.
